claims.text: Partial substitution of a PGM-based catalyst with a 3d transition metal alters the d-band center of its active sites.
Partial 3d-metal substitution alters the local coordination environment of the active metal sites.
The substitution-induced electronic and structural changes tune the adsorption energies of key intermediates on Pt.
Tuning intermediate adsorption energies lowers the surface coverage of CO-like poisoning species during ethanol oxidation.
The substituted catalyst facilitates hydrogenation steps in the ethanol oxidation pathway.
The substituted catalyst facilitates oxidative steps in the ethanol oxidation pathway.
Ethanol oxidation proceeds through a 12-electron, 12-proton pathway.
Partial 3d-metal substitution will produce higher ethanol-oxidation current density than an undoped Pt catalyst.
Partial 3d-metal substitution will improve stability over repeated ethanol-oxidation potential cycles.
Improved durability results from reduced coverage of poisoning intermediates.
The doped catalyst will show weaker in situ IR signals from adsorbed CO-like intermediates than undoped Pt.
In situ infrared spectroscopy can track the formation and consumption of ethanol-oxidation intermediates as potential and feed concentration are varied.
A potential range of 0.2–0.9 V versus RHE is a typical ethanol-oxidation operating window.
The proposed beneficial effect applies at moderate 3d-metal substitution levels below approximately 20 at.%.
The beneficial effect may diminish when the 3d-metal substitution exceeds an optimal range.
The beneficial effect may diminish outside standard ethanol-oxidation potential windows.
Electrolyte pH, temperature, and applied potential range may alter the predicted effect of 3d-metal substitution.

contradictions.description: The intervention field identifies in situ spectroscopy and variation of operating conditions as the intervention, whereas the baseline and falsification design treat 3d-metal doping as the controlled material change. Spectroscopy is a measurement rather than the change proposed to create the structural mediator.

The initial material is described as potentially already being a Pt alloy, while the hypothesis requires partial 3d-metal substitution and the decisive experiment compares a nominally 10% doped material with undoped PGM. The starting composition and substitution step are therefore not consistently defined.
